title: Constellation latency map: per-model & per-route p50/p95/p99 with streaming vs non-streaming breakdown
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Build a new visual dashboard (the "Constellation Map") to help SREs, infra and product owners quickly identify which model+route combinations are responsible for p50/p95/p99 latency spikes and whether the requests were streaming or non-streaming. The map is an interactive radial node graph where each node is a (model, route) pair sized by p99 and color-coded by streaming fraction. Clicking a node opens a detail panel with percentile time series, top trace samples (OTLP/Jaeger links), top errors, and suggested mitigation actions (cache, batching, fallback model).

Goals:
- Provide single-pane visibility for long-tail latency contributors across all models and routes.
- Surface streaming vs non-streaming splits in the same view and enable quick filtering.
- Link into trace samples and logs for rapid RCA.

Scope:
- Backend: aggregated histograms ingested from Prometheus/OpenTelemetry histograms or ClickHouse rollups. Compute p50/p95/p99 per model+route+io_mode every 1m and 5m.
- Traces: attach top-3 representative traces per node using trace similarity scoring from Tempo.
- Logs: show top error classes and recent stack traces from Loki/BigQuery.
- Frontend: implement Constellation radial layout in Console (React + d3) with interactive zoom, hover tooltips, and drill-in panel.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not cover long-term rollouts (A/B) or billing impact analysis; follow-ups will track those items.
acceptance_criteria: Constellation view renders for full traffic and for specified subset (model, route, env) within 30s
Each node displays p50/p95/p99 and streaming-fraction metric, and sizes by p99
Clicking node opens detail panel with last 1h percentile trend, 3 trace links, and top-5 error signatures
Backend exposes API endpoint (/api/observability/constellation) returning node list with metrics and links
Automated test that validates p99 calculation against histogram inputs for a synthetic workload
